questions.question: In which method of cooking is food heated slowly over a source of heat and cooked by high heat and air convection depending on the position of the food in relation to the fire?
questions.questionHtml: In which method of cooking is food heated slowly over a source of heat and cooked by high heat and air convection depending on the position of the food in relation to the fire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Spit-roasting.

  • In spit-roasting, the food is skewered on a spit and rotated slowly over a source of heat.
  • The heat source can be an open flame or hot coals, and the food is cooked by the radiant heat and hot air that surrounds it.
  • Spit-roasting is often used for large cuts of meat, such as whole chickens or pigs, and can result in a crispy, flavorful exterior and juicy interior.
  • This method of cooking requires constant attention and turning off the spit to ensure even cooking.

Braising

  • Braising involves cooking food slowly in a covered pot with a small amount of liquid, such as broth or wine.
  • The food is first seared on the stovetop to develop flavor, then simmered in the liquid for a long period of time.
  • This method is often used for tough cuts of meat, as the slow cooking and liquid help to tenderize the meat.
  • Braising can result in a flavorful, tender dish with a rich sauce.

Poaching

  • Poaching involves cooking food in a liquid that is just below boiling point.
  • The liquid can be water, broth, or other flavorful liquids, and the food is typically submerged in the liquid.
  • This method is often used for delicate foods, such as fish or eggs, as it is a gentle cooking method that helps to retain moisture and flavor.
  • Poaching can result in a tender, moist dish with a subtle flavor.

Stewing

  • Stewing involves cooking food slowly in a covered pot with a larger amount of liquid than braising.
  • The food is typically cut into smaller pieces and simmered in the liquid for a long period of time.
  • This method is often used for tougher cuts of meat, as the slow cooking and liquid help to tenderize the meat.
  • Stewing can result in a flavorful, tender dish with a rich sauce.

questions.question: In which of the following animal phyla, is the body divided into head, thorax and abdomen?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following animal phyla, is the body divided into head, thorax and abdomen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Arthropoda.
Key Points Arthropoda
  • Phylum Arthropoda is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom.
  • Over two-thirds of all named species on Earth are arthropods.
  • Phylum Arthropoda was first created by Von Seibold in 1845.
  • The body of arthropods is covered by a chitinous exoskeleton.
  • The body of arthropods consists of a head, thorax, and abdomen.
  • Phylum Arthropoda has jointed appendages.
  • The respiratory organs of arthropods are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system.
  • The circulatory system in Arthropoda is of open type.
  • Excretion in Arthropoda takes place through malpighian tubules.

Additional Information Annelida:

  • Annelida are aquatic or terrestrial, free-living, and sometimes parasitic.
  • They are coelomate. This allows true organs to be packaged in the body structure.
  • They are bilaterally symmetric and triploblastic.
  • Examples: Nereis - Hirudinaria.​

Chordata:

  • Animals belonging to phylum Chordata are fundamentally characterized by the presence of a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord, and paired pharyngeal gill slits.
  • They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, coelomate with the organ-system level of organization.
  • Phylum Chordata is divided into three subphyla: Urochordata or Tunicata, Cephalochordata, and Vertebrata.
  • Examples: Urochordata – Ascidia, Salpa, Doliolum; Cephalochordata – Amphioxus or Lancelet.

​Mollusca:

  • Example: Pila, Octopus
  • Excretion takes place through the kidneys.
  • Blood is colorless.
  • Respiration takes place through gills or ctenidia.
  • The alimentary canal is well developed.
  • The mantle is always present in it.
  • The body is divided into a head and a muscular foot.

questions.question: In which year did Antoine Lavoisier publish 'Methods of Chemical Nomenclature', which included the rules for naming chemical compounds that are still in use today?
questions.questionHtml: In which year did Antoine Lavoisier publish 'Methods of Chemical Nomenclature', which included the rules for naming chemical compounds that are still in use today?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1787.

Key Points

  • In 1787, four prominent French chemists – Louis Bernard Guyton de Morveau, Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier, Claude Louis Berthollet, and Antoine François Fourcroy – published a book with the title Méthode de nomenclature chimique.
  • In this book, they proposed a new nomenclature of chemical substances, explicated their principles of methodically constructing chemical names, and further presented a taxonomic table of chemical substances.
  • Historians of chemistry have unanimously praised the Method as a key document of eighteenth-century chemistry, particularly of Lavoisier’s epoch.
  • Since the nomenclatural and the taxonomic proposals of the Méthode were constructed in accordance with Lavoisier’s antiphlogistic chemical system, most historians have regarded it as a fruit and manifestation of this chemical system.

questions.question: Under Statutory liquidity ratio, commercial banks are required to keep a fraction of __________ in form of liquid assets.
questions.questionHtml: Under Statutory liquidity ratio, commercial banks are required to keep a fraction of __________ in form of liquid assets.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is total demand and term deposits.

Key Points

 Statutory liquidity ratio(SLR) is a government term where commercial banks are mandated to keep a specific proportion of total demand and term deposits in the form of liquid assets.

  • It is determined by the RBI.
  • It is used to control inflation and fuel growth, by decreasing or increasing the money supply.
  • Liquid Assets,  Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) and SLR Limit are the three components of SLR under Section 24 and Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act 1949.
  • Liquid Assets: Here assets like gold, security bonds can be easily converted to cash.
  • Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL): It refers to the total demand and time liabilities (deposits) of the public that are held by the banks with other banks.
  • Demand deposits consist of all liabilities, which the bank needs to pay on demand. They include current deposits, demand drafts etc.
  • Time deposits consist of deposits that will be repaid on maturity.
  • SLR Limit in India was a maximum of 40% and minimum of 20.75%. However, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) amended the Banking Regulation Act in January 2017 to remove the floor rate of 20.75% for SLR. This means that the RBI can now set the SLR at any level between 0% and 40%.
  • The RBI will incur a penalty on a bank if it does not keep the required SLR ratio.
  • SLR is calculated using the given formula: SLR rate = (liquid assets / (demand + time liabilities)) × 100%​

Additional Information Cash reserve ratio

  • The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is a monetary policy tool used by central banks, including the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), to regulate and control the money supply in the economy.
  • CRR is the percentage of total deposits that commercial banks are required to keep as reserves with the central bank.
  • It is a portion of the bank's demand and time liabilities.
  • The primary objective of implementing CRR is to ensure the liquidity and stability of the banking system while controlling inflation and managing credit growth.
  • When the central bank increases the CRR, it reduces the amount of money available for lending by commercial banks.
  • This helps reduce excess liquidity in the economy, controlling inflationary pressures, and curbing excessive credit expansion.
  • On the other hand, when the central bank decreases the CRR, it increases the amount of money available for lending by commercial banks.
  • This can stimulate credit growth, promote economic activity, and ease liquidity conditions in the economy.

  • The hysteresis curve allows us to select suitable materials for permanent magnets.
  • The hysteresis curve should be tall and wide for the material that is used to make a permanent magnet.
  • The material that is used to make a permanent magnet should have high retentivity and high coercivity.

    • They show almost complete accordance in their exposition of the “going of the cows” ceremony, the various soma ceremonies, and the different rites lasting from 1 to 12 days.

  • Yajurveda:
    • Yajurveda, collection of mantras (sacred formulas) and verses that forms part of the ancient sacred literature of India known as the Vedas.
    • Sacred formulas known as mantras were recited by the adhvaryu, the priest responsible for the sacrificial fire and for carrying out the ceremony.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right against Exploitation?
questions.questionHtml: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right against Exploitation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 23.

  • Article 23 deals with 'Right against Exploitation.

Key Points

  • Right against exploitation(Article 23-24).
  • Article 23 deals with the Prohibition of Human Trafficking and Forced Labour:
    • Forced labour in India was imposed by landlords, moneylenders and other wealthy persons in the past.
      • Article 23 of the Indian Constitution prohibits human trafficking and begar (forced labour without payment) to protect the millions of underprivileged and deprived people of the country.
      • The right is available to citizens of India as well as to non-citizens.
      • The right provides against human trafficking in the form of:
        • Selling and buying of men, women and children.
        • Prostitution
        • Devadasis
        • Slavery.
      • The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 13, 1956 has been enacted to deal with violations of this fundamental right.
  • Prohibition of Child Labour: Article 24 of the Indian Constitution forbids the employment of children below the age of 14 years in dangerous jobs like factories and mines.
    • However, it did not prohibit their employment in any harmless or innocent work.
    • The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (renamed as Child & Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 in 2016) specifically deals with the violations related to this right.
      • The 2016 amendment of this act completely prohibited the employment of children below 14 years of age in all occupations and processes.
      • It also prohibited the employment of adolescents (14-18 years of age) in hazardous occupations or processes.

Additional Information

  • Article 20 of the Constitution of India deals with the protection in respect of conviction for offences.
  • Article 22 deals with the protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.
  • Article 21 deals with the Protection of Life and Personal Liberty.

questions.question: By which of the following acts was a bicameral legislature introduced in India at the centre level?

questions.solution:

Key Points

  • Government of India Act, 1919
    • The matters, which were of National importance or related to more than one province were governed at the central level, such as Foreign Affairs, Defence, Political Relations, Communication, Public Debt, Civil and Criminal Laws, Wire services, etc.
    • The Central Legislature was made more powerful and more representative by this Act.
    • The Act introduced a bicameral legislature; the Lower House or Central Legislative Assembly and the Upper House or Council of State.
    • The legislators, under the new reforms, could now ask questions and supplementary, pass adjournment motions, and vote a part of the budget, but 75% of the budget was still not votable.
    • The legislature had virtually no control over the Governor-General and his Executive Council.

Additional Information

  • Government of India Act 1935
    • There was a growing demand for constitutional reforms in India by Indian leaders.
    • India’s support to Britain in the First World War also aided in British acknowledgment of the need for the inclusion of more Indians in the administration of their own country.
    • The Act was based on
      • Simon Commission Report
      • The recommendations of the Round Table Conferences
      • The White Paper published by the British government in 1933 (based on the Third Round Table Conference)
      • Report of the Joint Select Committees.
  • Morley-Minto Reforms 1909
    • The legislative councils at the Centre and the provinces increased in size.
    • Central Legislative Council – from 16 to 60 members.
    • Legislative Councils of Bengal, Madras, Bombay, and United Provinces – 50 members each.
    • Legislative Councils of Punjab, Burma, and Assam – 30 members each.
    • The legislative councils at the Centre and the provinces were to have four categories of members as follows:
      • Ex officio members: Governor-General and members of the executive council.
      • Nominated official members: Government officials who were nominated by the Governor-General.
      • Nominated non-official members: nominated by the Governor-General but were not government officials.
      • Elected members: elected by different categories of Indians.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase. Though very rich, Alexander always saves for a rainy day.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase.

Though very rich, Alexander always saves for a rainy day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Saves money for later.

Key Points

  • The phrase "saves for a rainy day" is an idiom. Idioms are expressions whose meanings cannot be inferred from the meanings of the words that make them up. This particular idiom means to save money for a time when it might be needed unexpectedly, such as during an emergency or in times of difficulty, which could be referred to metaphorically as a "rainy day."
  • Therefore, in the context of the sentence "Though very rich, Alexander always saves for a rainy day," it indicates that despite his wealth, Alexander is cautious and saves money for future unforeseen expenses.

Thus, the first option, "Saves money for later," is the most appropriate as it directly relates to the meaning of the idiom.

 Additional Information

  • "Lives like a miser" implies extreme frugality, which is not the same as saving for future needs.
  • "Spends too much" is the opposite of the idiom's meaning.
  • "Accumulates less wealth" does not align with the concept of saving; it suggests not gaining wealth, not saving it.

According to him, Rupees 75 lakhs has been spent to make the gymnasium fully equipped with state-of-the-art fitness machines. B. Mr. Mercia, the Principal of the school familiarised the guests about the cost incurred and the various facilities available.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. According to him, Rupees 75 lakhs has been spent to make the gymnasium fully equipped with state-of-the-art fitness machines.

B. The Honorable Commissioner of Police inaugurated the Gymnasium and Swimming pool and appended the management for their efforts in providing such amenities to students.

C. A new indoor gymnasium and swimming pool was inaugurated at APJ International School, Goa.

D. Mr. Mercia, the Principal of the school familiarised the guests about the cost incurred and the various facilities available.
questions.solution:
The correct order is: CBDA.

Key Points

  • The opening sentence should introduce the topic, which in this case is the inauguration of a new facility.
  • Sentence C does this by mentioning the inauguration of the gymnasium and swimming pool.
  • Following the introduction of the event in sentence C, the next logical step is to mention who inaugurated the facility, which is provided in sentence B.
  • Once the event and the dignitary are introduced, the next detail often includes additional information about the event or comments made during it. Sentence D provides this by detailing the Principal's actions during the event.
  • Finally, sentence A gives specific information about the investment made, which is usually mentioned after the formalities of introduction and inauguration are covered.

Therefore, the correct order is: CBDA

Additional Information

  • Starting with costs (A) or facility details (C) is less logical without first introducing the event (B).
  • Sequences that do not start with B (the inauguration) lack a clear and logical introduction.

  • The prefix "auto-" means "self," and "biography" is the written record of someone's life. Hence, "autobiography" is the life history written by oneself. (आत्मकथा)
    • ​For example: The celebrity penned an autobiography detailing her rise to fame.

Therefore, the correct one-word substitute for "Life history written by oneself" is "Autobiography."

Additional Information

  • Autography: This word refers to a person's own handwriting or signature, not their life history. (अनुवाद) 
    • ​For example: Her autography revealed a fascinating, yet previously unknown aspect of her life.
  • Autophagy: A biological term that means the destruction of cells within the body during normal physiological processes. (भोजी)
    • ​For example: Autophagy is a cellular process where cells digest parts of themselves for energy.
  • Autocracy: A system of government by one person with absolute power, not related to life history or writing. ("एकतन्त्र)
    • For example: The country was under the rule of an autocracy where one person held absolute power.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. You should / see a oculist; / your eyes look / worse today.

You should / see a oculist; / your eyes look / worse today.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'see a oculist'.

Key Points

  • The mistake in the sentence lies in the segment "see a oculist;" where the indefinite article "a" is used incorrectly before a vowel sound.
  • The correct indefinite article to use before a word that starts with a vowel sound is "an," not "a."
  • So, the corrected segment should be "see an oculist;" to properly align with the rules of English grammar regarding the usage of articles.

​Therefore, the correct sentence is: "You should see an oculist; your eyes look worse today."

Additional Information

  • "A" is used before words that begin with a consonant sound, while "an" is used before words that begin with a vowel sound.
  • This rule is based on sound, not spelling, so the use of "a" or "an" is determined by the pronunciation of the word that follows it.
  • For example, we say "a university" (because 'university' begins with a 'yoo' sound, which is a consonant sound) and "an hour" (because 'hour' starts with a silent 'h' and therefore the first sound is 'ow', which is a vowel sound).

Additional Information

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. This has an impact not just on global poverty, but also on Indians' awareness of the country's poverty for the first time in a decade. B. And, for the first time in a decade, this update includes India's poverty data. C. From 15 September 2022, a new global poverty line has been established, with the World Bank revising its data in the Poverty and Inequality Platform on this basis. D. According to Sunitha Sinha, Roy and Roy van der Weide of the World Bank's Policy Research Working Paper, "poverty in India had dropped over the recent decade, although not as much as previously thought."
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. This has an impact not just on global poverty, but also on Indians' awareness of the country's poverty for the first time in a decade.

B. And, for the first time in a decade, this update includes India's poverty data.

C. From 15 September 2022, a new global poverty line has been established, with the World Bank revising its data in the Poverty and Inequality Platform on this basis.

D. According to Sunitha Sinha, Roy and Roy van der Weide of the World Bank's Policy Research Working Paper, "poverty in India had dropped over the recent decade, although not as much as previously thought."
questions.solution:
The correct order is 'CBAD'.

Key Points

  • Sentence C introduces a new development concerning the global poverty line, making it a natural starting point for the paragraph.
  • Sentence B elaborates on the new development mentioned in sentence C by adding the detail that this update includes India's poverty data for the first time in a decade.
  • Sentence A builds on sentence B by explaining the impact of this new global poverty line on both global poverty and Indians' awareness of their country's poverty.
  • Sentence D provides a specific statement from experts, which serves as supporting information to the details given in sentences A and B.

Therefore, the correct order is CBAD.

Additional Information

  • Sequence DBAC starts with expert commentary, which is less effective without the context of the new poverty line.
  • Sequence CADB introduces the impact on India before the new poverty line has been established, which disrupts the logical flow.
  • Sequence DBCA again leads with commentary and follows with an alternative name, which is not coherent as the name should come after introducing the festival.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Were the cakes being baked by them?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Were they baking the cakes?

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in the passive voice, with the subject 'the cakes' receiving the action of being baked by 'them'.
  • To convert to active voice, the subject performing the action ('they') should be at the beginning of the sentence.

Thus, the sentence in active voice corresponding to "Were the cakes being baked by them?" is "Were they baking the cakes?"

  • Option 4 "Was cakes being baked by them?" is grammatically incorrect due to the singular verb "was" with the plural noun "cakes."

questions.question: Choose the ANTONYM of the word 'disenfranchise' in the given sentence. The parliament of Tonoco authorised the king to take over the reins of the government and disable the power of the council of ministers.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the ANTONYM of the word 'disenfranchise' in the given sentence.

The parliament of Tonoco authorised the king to take over the reins of the government and disable the power of the council of ministers.
questions.solution:
The correct option is: Authorised.

Key Points

  • "Disenfranchise" means to deprive someone of the right to vote or of power, rights, or privileges. (नागरिकता से वंचित करना)
  • "Authorised" means to give legal or official approval to do something, which is the opposite of deprivation. ("अधिकृत)
    • ​For example: The board authorised the new policy during the last meeting.
  • Thus, the parliament authorising the king implies granting him powers or rights, which is the opposite of disenfranchising.

Therefore, the correct answer is Authorised.

Additional Information

  • "Disabled" is similar in meaning to "disenfranchise" as it can imply being deprived of certain abilities or functions. (विकलांग)
    • For example: The accident left him disabled and unable to work.
  • "Powers" is not the direct antonym of "disenfranchise" but rather a related concept. Disenfranchisement often involves the removal of powers, but "powers" itself does not imply the act of granting rights.
    • ​For example: The constitution divides powers between the federal and state governments.
  • "Reins" metaphorically relates to control or guidance and does not directly oppose "disenfranchise."
    • ​​For example: When he retired, he handed over the reins of the company to his daughter.
  • The phrase "take over the reins" does imply gaining control, but "reins" alone does not constitute an antonym for disenfranchise.
